requirement:
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:

```text
Acknowledgment {
    file: String,
    item: String,
    body: String,
    issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
}
```

`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.

The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.

Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`, and the assertions would catch a violation of each one. I found no gaps. I did not read implementation source.

- **Inclusion, exclusion and validity.**
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes]` checks that a named fixme becomes exactly one acknowledgment with file `src/lib.rs`, item `fn[gap]` and body `The gap.`. It also checks that an unnamed fixme is not supplied.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[acknowledgment_metadata_is_ordered_and_deduplicates_issue_options]` writes four invalid fixmes (unsupported option, malformed issue, empty body, unclosed fence). It checks that none are supplied, because only 3 entries come back.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cited_built_ins_contribute_their_text_and_fixmes_in_own_sites_do_not]` checks the exclusion for the subject's own sites. A fixme inside a site is left out, and only the fixme in `fn[other]` is supplied.
- **Form of the entry.**
  - The `<root>` item is asserted for a plain-text file in the metadata test.
  - The `fn[...]` items are asserted in the ordering and site tests.
  - Bodies keep their option lines, with the `:github:` lines and their duplicates preserved in the metadata test. Comment delimiters are stripped, as the `// ` prefixes are absent from the bodies in the ordering test.
  - Redaction is checked in `acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads`, where a GitHub token becomes `[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` asserts the exact JSON entry for a requirement subject. For an example subject it asserts an empty list.
- **Issues.**
  - The metadata test asserts distinct issues in the order of the `:github:` lines (`#2`, then `#1`, with the repeated `#2` dropped). It also asserts the default state `open` when GitHub is unreachable.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[initial_acknowledgments_supply_closed_and_missing_issue_states_without_source]` checks that `closed` is supplied for both `example/queue#125` and `example/queue#404` through a fake GitHub server.
- **Ordering and no source or line numbers.**
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[acknowledgment_order_follows_file_then_source_position_even_when_names_sort_backwards]` uses `src/a.rs` with `zeta` before `alpha`, then `src/z.rs`. This separates file order and source-position order from name order.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` asserts that the metadata carries no `line_start` or `line_end`.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[initial_acknowledgments_supply_closed_and_missing_issue_states_without_source]` asserts `pub fn beta()` is absent from the prompt. `acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads` asserts `IMPLEMENTATION_BODY` is absent.
- **Staleness and the reference-set digest.**
  - `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[editing_or_adding_a_fixme_makes_evidence_stale_without_requiring_source_reads]` shows that editing a fixme body, or adding a fixme in another file, reports `reference set changed`.
  - The same test shows no `outline input changed` error and no `no input covers {fixme}` error.
  - `acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads` shows that an edit to the unread containing body leaves validation clean.
- **No outline input created merely to cover the containing source.** The metadata test asserts that no mandatory input has a `file`. The site test and the definitions test assert that no input has an `item`.
- **Actual reads still recorded.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[implementation_discovery_has_no_text_or_evidence_until_the_model_requests_a_read]` shows that a later `read_node` of `fn[ready]` adds exactly one outline input.
- **Inaccessible source.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[inaccessible_acknowledgment_source_aborts_preparation]` makes the file unreadable. It asserts that preparation fails with `gap.rs` and `Permission denied` in the error, so the failure comes before inference.
- **Definitions.**
  - `acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads` has a body that references `terms.boundary`, which references `terms.unit`.
  - It asserts that both complete declarations are supplied, including the phrase option. It also asserts that validation detects a change to the transitive `terms.unit` and a missing definition input.
  - The containing source is not supplied.

The tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. The one case I note but do not treat as a gap is an example subject that has its own fixme. It is only checked as an empty list. The requirement text does not distinguish requirement and example handling, so a separate test is not needed.

text: :::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
:::{req} discovery
Habeas MUST find the references of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
in project source files, where {cite}`requirements.references.reference_contexts`
says they count, and MUST fail with the source file and line if a
name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped
roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST scan current files under the project directory, including
new files as soon as they are created. It MUST respect `.gitignore` files in the
project, including nested rules and exceptions, in projects with or without Git.
It MUST skip the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git` and `target`
at any depth, and paths disallowed by {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`.
Evidence snapshots and
generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
:::{req} site_review
Every site of a distributed requirement under
{cite}`requirements.references.distributed` MUST have a site review: an
assessment of whether that site upholds the requirement, recorded at
`evidence/sites/<full-name>/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` and
`<selector>` are encoded as under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. The review MUST use the prompt
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.site_prompt`. Mandatory inputs, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the site's outline
node, the requirement's complete declaration, and each declaration the
requirement cites. The record MUST contain the requirement's full name, the
site's file and selector, `queries`, the sorted names of the queries with a
match at the site, `applies`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`, with
determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. `applies` MUST be a
Boolean recording whether the requirement applies to the site. A site to which
the requirement does not apply MUST be judged `true`, and the rationale MUST
explain why it does not apply. `habeas info` MUST report, for each selected
distributed requirement, how many of its sites the requirement does not apply
to.
Validation MUST require a current, accepted review for every site, MUST report a
false review with its rationale, and MUST report stale, missing, or orphaned
reviews; a review is orphaned when its file and selector no longer name a site
of the requirement. A `{fixme}` naming the requirement inside a site
acknowledges a gap at that site only: it MUST be an input to that site's review
and MUST NOT contribute to the requirement's own review, coverage, or reference
set. A review MUST become stale when the site's hash, the requirement's
declaration, a cited declaration, its `queries`, or the `{fixme}` references
naming the requirement inside the site, with the words of their bodies, change.
Each site review's determination MUST be checked on its own, independently of
the requirement's evidence. Authoring with `--all` MUST include site reviews,
`habeas author sites:<full-name>` MUST author the site reviews of the named
requirement, and `habeas author sites:<full-name>/<file>#<selector>` MUST author
the review of the one site it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>` names the
file's root node. `habeas status` MUST report missing, stale, invalid, and false
site reviews with their requirement, file, and selector, and `habeas info` MUST
list each selected requirement's sites with their determinations.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
:::{req} redaction
Habeas MUST apply the SDK's built-in credential rules to source text supplied
in mandatory inputs, tool reads, and search results, and to source text shown
in the book and `habeas info`. The same rules apply to configuration files.
Each match of a built-in `secretshape` rule MUST be replaced with
`[REDACTED:<rule name>]`, preserving every line break. The match MUST extend
through adjacent regions flagged by the entropy heuristic when only whitespace
separates them. Entropy alone MUST NOT trigger a replacement.
Outlines MUST use the original source for structure and spans. Structural
hashes MUST use the redacted text for each matched region as specified in
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.redaction`. The `secretshape` version MUST be
pinned exactly because changes to its rules can affect evidence hashes.
:::{req} github_reads
The harness MUST expose a `github` tool with this interface:
```text
github({ issue: String }) -> Issue
Issue { reference: String, state: "open" | "closed", title: String, body: String }
`issue` MUST have the form `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`. The tool MUST read the issue
or pull request through the GitHub API, authenticating with the `GITHUB_TOKEN`
environment variable when that is set, and MUST return its body redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. GitHub reads cannot be reproduced
later, so their results MUST NOT be recorded as evidence inputs and MUST NOT
make evidence stale. Every GitHub read by Habeas, including this tool's, the
lookups below, and those of {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`, MUST go
through one cache under the state root of
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`, keyed by issue, and MUST
reuse a cached result less than one hour old instead of contacting GitHub. A malformed reference, a missing issue, or a failed request
MUST return an explanatory tool error.
When the mandatory inputs contain a `{fixme}` reference under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, or the initial request includes one under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`, the harness MUST look up the state of
each issue its `:github:` lines name in the same way and MUST supply each state
with the corresponding source input or acknowledgment as `open` or `closed`;
when GitHub cannot be reached, the issue MUST be assumed open. These states MUST

NOT be recorded either. Instead, `habeas status` and `habeas author` MUST treat a recorded FIXME determination as stale, exactly as if one of its inputs had changed, when an issue that one of its acknowledging `{fixme}` references names, or for a site review the `{fixme}` references inside the site, is closed or does not exist; repository validation, which never contacts GitHub, MUST NOT.
The harness MAY take the GitHub API base URL from `HABEAS_GITHUB_API_URL`,
accepting only `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, so that tests can use a local server.
:::{req} reference_set

A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` edges, except a `{fixme}` inside a site of the definition under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node, and, for a fenced reference in a source outside the book, the words of
its body under the word rule of {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
`{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
For a structural assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, the digest MUST additionally
include a versioned structural-assessment marker. A record predating structural
assessment MUST therefore be stale, including a legacy record with a wildcard
review version. Other assessments MUST retain their existing digest encoding.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, editing its commentary, or moving it to a different node
MUST therefore make the evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
:::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records

itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later. For citation assessments, additional node reads and selected excerpts are recorded as SDK dependencies under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
:::{req} source_tools

All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools. A read uses the node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`. A delivered read records that node’s fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. The source project follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read refers to a terminology definition, the agent can
read its declaration with `read_node` using the definition's domain identity.
The SDK records each definition the agent reads.
